newsitem.title: FRANCE: More French areas restrict water despite rain.
newsitem.headline: More French areas restrict water despite rain.

text.p: Despite recent rain, seven new French departments or provinces have added water restrictions to cope with low supplies caused by four months of dry weather, the environment ministry said on Friday.

The irrigation and other restrictions were drawn up between April 30 and May 6 and cover two maize-producing areas in the southwest, two other cereals zones in the north and three agro-food production areas in western France.
France's overseas territory of Guadeloupe is also affected, bringing to 25 the number of departments touched by water restrictions since early April.
There are roughly 100 such administrative areas in France, including four overseas.

Ministry officials said the latest restrictions applied to the following departments -- Aisne and Seine-Maritime in the north, Gironde and Lot-et-Garonne in the southwest and Ille-et-Vilaine, Loire-Atlantique and Sarthe in the west.
Dordogne in the southwest, which had been on the list for possible restrictions, has so far been spared a clampdown.
Weather experts say a bout of rainfall since last weekend has improved crop conditions on the surface but underground water tables are still up to 50 percent below normal levels.
Most of the 17 areas which have already had water restrictions in force since early April are key cereals growing areas in the north and south of the Paris grain basin.
The 17 are Calvados, Charente, Cher, Cote-d'Or, Essonne, Eure, Eure-et-Loir, Indre, Loir-et-Cher, Loiret, Oise, Orne, Pas-de-Calais, Seine-et-Marne, Somme, Yvelines and Vendee.
